recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not move profile-specific vital-sign identifiers into Observation.category unless a future work-group decision explicitly reopens that breaking change; separate cross-paradigm or IG-specific vital-sign model work belongs in separate trackers or repositories.
issue_request: FHIR-45617 was Applied/Not Persuasive with Modification for R6. It proposed moving vital-sign-specific LOINC grouping identifiers from Observation.code to Observation.category to avoid semantic ambiguity when a more detailed measurement code is also present, but the final decision rejected that breaking move and instead required guidance that the mandated standard code can be accompanied by a more detailed coding plus preferred broader LOINC bindings.
initial_application: Jira records applied git 66a80b5fef2c43d4a46709f2a03b6d933063cb08. That commit moved the Vital Signs interoperability standard LOINC codes back from Observation.category to Observation.code, updated the vital signs introduction, removed the temporary observation-vitalsign-category value set, and changed the affected Observation examples/profile differentials.
additional_context: The affected files are current build inputs: fhir.ini lists Observation, the Observation packs list includes ImplementationGuide/Observation-vitalsigns, and that guide is marked core and references the vital-sign profiles. Related applied category-vs-code issues FHIR-49953, FHIR-50689, and FHIR-50705 are already represented on the combined branch, and community searches found OO discussion of the same debate without a conflicting final decision.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current prose says standard vital-sign codes may be accompanied by more detailed Observation.code.coding values, the base Vital Signs profile binds Observation.code to observation-vitalsign-measurement with preferred strength, each specific vital-sign profile patterns its standard LOINC code in Observation.code and has a preferred observation-vitalsign-* binding, and stale category-code searches found no remaining source-backed contradiction.
